name: PHP
short: The source code of the PHP interpreter, with steps to build it, test it and install it yourself.
what: php-src is the official repository for PHP, the general-purpose scripting language used across web development. The README covers prebuilt packages, building PHP from source on Ubuntu, Fedora and macOS, running the test suite, and installing extensions with PIE.
who: Developers who want to build PHP themselves, test a change or contribute to the language. If you only want to run PHP, use a prebuilt package from windows.php.net or the installation chapter on php.net.
needs: For a minimal build from Git: autoconf, bison and re2c
For a default build, also libxml2 and libsqlite3
A C build toolchain (the Ubuntu command installs build-essential)

steps.title: Get a prebuilt package
steps.text: If you only need PHP, skip the build. On Windows, get the binaries from windows.php.net. After you extract the archive the `.exe` files are ready to use. For other systems, see the installation chapter at php.net/install.

steps.title: Install the build tools
steps.text: This is the Ubuntu command. The README also gives commands for Fedora, Homebrew and MacPorts.
steps.code: sudo apt install -y pkg-config build-essential autoconf bison re2c libxml2-dev libsqlite3-dev

steps.title: Configure the build
steps.text: `--enable-debug` is recommended for development. `./configure --help` lists every option.

steps.title: Build it
steps.text: Set the job count to roughly your number of cores, which `nproc` shows.

try.label: From the README
try.text: After building, test one directory only: `make TESTS=tests/lang/ test`

watch: `make install` may need superuser permissions, depending on your permissions and install prefix.
Windows builds from source follow a separate guide on the PHP wiki.
New features need an accepted RFC. Bug fixes don't.
